title: The filioque
hookLine: Western churches added and the Son to the creed about the Spirit; the Orthodox did not, and the argument continues gently

lines: FROM THE FATHER AND THE SON.
cards: Sunday morning, two churches on the same street. In one, the people say the Nicene Creed, and when they reach the Holy Spirit they say: who proceeds from the Father and the Son.
Across the street, in an Orthodox church, the people say the same creed, and at the same spot they say: who proceeds from the Father. Same creed. Same Spirit.
A difference of a few words in English, and in Latin, just one. That word has a long story. Today's word: filioque.

teach.b: Filioque is Latin for and the Son. The Nicene Creed, as the early councils agreed it in Greek, said the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father.
That echoes Jesus at the Last Supper in John's Gospel: "the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father." In the West, where the church prayed in Latin, churches came to add filioque.
The English prayer book carries it: "Who proceedeth from the Father and the Son." Catholic and Anglican churches, among others in the West, have said it that way.

Orthodox Christians say the creed without it, for two reasons. A creed agreed by the whole church shouldn't be changed by one part of it. And they speak of the Father as the one source within the Trinity.

teach.h: WHOM I WILL SEND UNTO YOU.
teach.b: Western teachers answer that the word guards the bond between the Son and the Spirit, and point to the very same verse, where Jesus says of the Spirit, "whom I will send unto you from the Father."
The Son sends; the Spirit proceeds from the Father. Orthodox teachers reply that sending in time is not proceeding in eternity. Each side leans on a different half.
This one word became one of the disagreements in the long, painful parting between East and West, and it's still not settled.
But in recent times the tone has grown gentler, with Catholic and Orthodox leaders talking it through patiently, and some Western churches leaving the word out when they pray alongside the Orthodox.

how: Catholic, Anglican and other Western churches say in the Nicene Creed that the Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son; Orthodox churches say from the Father, keeping the creed's older wording.

games.q: you're at the Last Supper, and Jesus is speaking about the Spirit of truth who is coming. where does he say the Spirit proceeds from?
games.why: "the Spirit of truth, which proceedeth from the Father." in the same verse he says he will send the Spirit from the Father. Western readers lean on the sending; Orthodox readers say sending in time is not proceeding in eternity.

practice: Say the line quietly in the Western form: I believe in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and giver of life, who proceedeth from the Father and the Son.

Then say the Eastern form, stopping at from the Father, and notice what changes and how much stays the same. Hold in mind the people who will say each one this Sunday; if you pray, you can pray for both.

wordCard.voice: Filioque. Latin for and the Son: one word Western churches say in the creed and the Orthodox do not.

carryVoice: Your line: one word, long argument. These days, it's held more carefully. I'll be here tomorrow.
